author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can cancel an upcoming visit from the owner's record
summary: A visit booked against the wrong pet or the wrong day can be withdrawn from the owner's record. The cancel action is offered only against a visit dated later than today; a visit dated today or earlier carries none.
acceptance_criteria: given a pet with a visit dated later than today, when the owner's record is opened, then that visit is shown with a cancel action beside it
given a pet with a visit dated today or earlier, when the owner's record is opened, then that visit is shown with no cancel action beside it
given an upcoming visit, when it is cancelled, then the owner's record is shown again without that visit among the pet's visits
given an upcoming visit, when it is cancelled, then every other visit of that pet and of every other pet is left untouched
given a visit dated today or earlier, when its cancellation is requested directly, then the request is refused and the visit stands
given a visit belonging to a pet of another owner, when its cancellation is requested, then the request is refused and the visit stands
given the cancel action's wording, when the supported languages are checked, then it is present in every one of them
edge case 3: a visit dated exactly today is not upcoming, so it carries no cancel action and cannot be cancelled
edge case 4: a request to cancel a visit that is no longer held leaves the pet's record unchanged
edge case 5: cancelling a pet's only visit leaves that pet shown with no visits, not removed from the record
non_goals: NG-10: retaining a cancelled visit, or any visit status the record carries
NG-11: cancelling a visit dated today or earlier
changing a visit's date or description once booked (NG-5, unchanged)
deleting an owner or a pet (NG-4, unchanged)
asking for confirmation before the cancellation takes effect — left as an open question in the PRD, not decided
notes: Minted REQ-VIS-003: REQ-VIS-002 was already taken by the earlier-visits-shown-when-booking requirement. A stale dispatch-start at line 1 names REQ-VIS-002 and is superseded by line 2. Boundary decision: the upcoming-only rule reuses REQ-VIS-001's existing later-than-today boundary rather than inventing a second one; rationale is in the non-goal ADR, not the PRD. The request contradicted NG-4 and NG-5, both derived from absence during the 2026-07-31 survey and flagged in the PRD as an open consultation; both are narrowed rather than silently overridden. Eleven message bundles carry the new cancel wording (REQ-LANG-002).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: First removal the application performs; every existing write is an insert or update. Cancellation enters through the Owner aggregate root, matching the sole-write-path invariant in system-design.md#contracts, and the visits association gains orphanRemoval. The upcoming rule lives on Visit and Pet, not in a controller, because architecture-principles.md's Web controller row admits no new business rule and the view needs the same predicate. Recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-07-cancelling-a-visit-through-the-owner-aggregate.md; the product boundary is already settled by the non-goal ADR.
integration_points: new route POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/cancel, redirecting to /owners/{ownerId} on both outcomes
Visit gains isUpcoming(); the ownerDetails template reads it as ${visit.upcoming} to decide whether to render the action
Pet gains cancelVisit(visitId) returning whether the visit was withdrawn; Owner gains cancelVisit(petId, visitId) delegating to it
one new message key for the cancel action's label, added to all eleven bundles under src/main/resources/messages/

patterns.description: Owner.addVisit(petId, visit) is the mirror to follow for cancelVisit. One asymmetry is deliberate: addVisit asserts on an unknown pet, cancelVisit returns false so an identifier for another owner's pet is refused rather than routed to the error page.
existing shape for a visit POST handler: mutate the owner aggregate, owners.save(owner), redirect to the owner record
the per-visit row in the visits table is where the cancel action attaches; it must be an inline form with method=post, not an anchor

risks.risk: VisitController declares @ModelAttribute("visit") loadPetWithVisit, which runs before every handler in that class and calls pet.addVisit(new Visit()). A cancellation handler placed in VisitController would save an owner carrying that phantom transient visit; its @NotBlank description then fails at flush.
risks.mitigation: put the handler in a new VisitCancellationController in the same package, which declares no shared model attribute. Do not add the route to VisitController.

risks.risk: Without orphanRemoval, removing a visit from the collection nulls pet_id instead of deleting the row. pet_id is nullable on h2, mysql, and postgres, so the detach succeeds silently and an orphan row survives, contradicting NG-10. Every test that reads through the owner's object graph still passes.
risks.mitigation: set orphanRemoval = true on Pet.visits, and assert the deletion at the persistence level (row count over visits, in the style of ClinicServiceTests) rather than only through MockMvc.

risks.risk: BaseEntity declares no equals or hashCode, so the LinkedHashSet holding visits uses identity equality. A constructed probe Visit will never be removed.
risks.mitigation: locate the visit by comparing getId() and remove the located instance.

risks.risk: Visit.isUpcoming() reads LocalDate.now() directly, an implicit clock dependency.
risks.mitigation: consistent with the existing Visit constructor and VisitController; tests date their fixtures relative to LocalDate.now() rather than pinning a Clock.

risks.risk: This is the first destructive route in an application with no authentication and no CSRF protection.
risks.mitigation: POST-only, and the aggregate refuses any pet or visit the named owner does not hold. The posture itself is unchanged by this slice and stays recorded in system-design.md#security-context; do not invent an auth control here.

notes: Verdict new. Durable memory written: docs/adr/2026-08-07-cancelling-a-visit-through-the-owner-aggregate.md (new, indexed in docs/adr/README.md); docs/system-design.md updated in Package Structure, Contracts (Owner, Pet, Visit rows plus a new VisitCancellationController row), Persistence, Security Context, and Threat Model (one row amended, one added). No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty. Refusal shape: all three refusal cases (visit dated today or earlier, pet or visit not held by this owner, visit no longer held) redirect to the owner's record leaving it unchanged; none throws. Routing a refusal through IllegalArgumentException would reach the error page, which renders exception text (a Known Defect against REQ-SYS-002). No confirmation step is designed in, per the PRD's open question; the POST form leaves room for one. Deliberate omission worth the human's attention: the slice adds no flash confirmation or refusal text. No acceptance criterion asks for it, and all eight existing flash messages in the owner package are hard-coded English, which breaches REQ-LANG-002. That pre-existing breach is systemic and out of this slice's scope, but it is a defect nobody has recorded; a separate slice should either translate those eight or record the gap.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: cancelVisit resolves the Optional<Owner> with the isPresent()/get() pair (`if (optionalOwner.isPresent()) { Owner owner = optionalOwner.get(); ... }`). This is the only isPresent()/get() call site in src/main/java in the whole codebase — every other Optional<Owner> from OwnerRepository.findById (OwnerController, PetController, VisitController) is resolved with orElseThrow, and the codebase otherwise favors functional Optional idioms per the checklist. orElseThrow would change behavior here (the ADR wants a silent refusal, not a thrown exception), but the imperative isPresent()/get() pair is still avoidable without changing behavior.
findings.fix: Replace with `this.owners.findById(ownerId).filter(owner -> owner.cancelVisit(petId, visitId)).ifPresent(this.owners::save);` (or an equivalent ifPresent/map chain) so the method reads as a single Optional pipeline consistent with the rest of the package.

approved_aspects: Visit.isUpcoming, Pet.cancelVisit and Owner.cancelVisit each carry a clear single responsibility and a Javadoc that states the refusal semantics precisely
Pet.cancelVisit's comment on locating-then-removing the held instance (BaseEntity has no value equality) heads off a subtle correctness bug a future editor could reintroduce
VisitCancellationController is correctly kept separate from VisitController to avoid saving the phantom @ModelAttribute visit, and is documented as such
Message bundle updates are complete and consistently placed across all eleven bundles (base plus nine live translations, messages_en left empty per its own convention)
Template change is minimal, uses the existing __${}__ URL-expression convention, and gates the form on visit.upcoming exactly as the domain method defines it
./gradlew checkFormat passes with no findings

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: The design-block's claim that the security posture is unchanged holds for the CONTROLS but not for the IMPACT of their absence, and the difference is a human decision. Controls: unchanged and correctly assessed. Mutating POST routes already exist unauthenticated (/owners/new, /owners/{id}/edit, /pets/new, /pets/{petId}/edit, /visits/new), the application carries no Spring Security dependency and no CSRF token anywhere, and this slice adds no new class of exposure. Impact: newly worsened. POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/cancel is the first route in the application that DESTROYS persisted state rather than creating or amending it — Pet.visits now carries orphanRemoval = true, so the row is deleted, and NG-10 declines any retained cancelled visit, so there is no soft-delete, no undo, and no audit record of who cancelled what. Two concrete attack paths follow from the absent controls: (a) direct — any caller who can reach the application enumerates ownerId/petId/visitId (small sequential integers) and permanently deletes every upcoming visit in the clinic, unauthenticated; (b) cross-site — with no CSRF token, any page a staff browser loads can auto-submit this form to an internal-only deployment and delete visits the attacker cannot otherwise reach. Both were bounded to data CREATION and AMENDMENT before this slice; they now reach irreversible data LOSS. No code fix is prescribed here: inventing an auth or CSRF control inside this slice would be a design decision the design-block deliberately declined, and it is out of the requirement's scope. The human call is whether an unauthenticated, CSRF-unprotected, irreversible destructive route is acceptable for this deployment, or whether the slice should be gated behind a separate security slice (Spring Security with CSRF enabled, or a soft-delete/status column that makes cancellation recoverable). The system-design threat model already records the exposure honestly in its first row, including the phrase 'Cancellation is the one destructive route, and it is reachable on the same terms' — the escalation is the decision, not the documentation.

approved_aspects: IDOR is genuinely prevented, verified against the code rather than the design's claim: VisitCancellationController resolves the Owner by path ownerId, then Owner.cancelVisit delegates to Owner.getPet(Integer) (Owner.java:117), which iterates only this owner's own pets collection and matches on identity; Pet.cancelVisit then resolves the visit only within that pet's own visits collection (Pet.findVisit). A petId or visitId held by another owner resolves to null and returns false. VisitCancellationControllerTests.cancellingAVisitOfAnotherOwnersPetShouldBeRefused pins it, asserting the other owner's visit survives and save() is never called.

The upcoming-only rule is enforced server-side in the domain (Pet.cancelVisit checks held.isUpcoming()), not merely gated in the template's th:if. A forged POST against a visit dated today or earlier is refused at the aggregate — the template gating is presentation, not the control.

Refusals are indistinguishable from successes to the caller: every outcome returns the same redirect to /owners/{ownerId} with no flash text, so the route leaks no existence oracle for pets or visits held by other owners. Refusals also never call save(), so no partial write escapes.

No injection in the new native query. ClinicServiceTests.countVisitRowsWithId uses a positional bind parameter ('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM visits WHERE id = ?1' with setParameter(1, visitId)) over an Integer — no string concatenation, no interpolation, and the value is not user-derived. Swept the whole source tree with grep -F for createNativeQuery and createQuery: this is the only native query in src/, production or test.

Output escaping holds in ownerDetails.html. The new cells render through th:text (escaped by Thymeleaf's default) and the new form's th:action is an @{} link expression over Integer identifiers (owner.id, pet.id, visit.id), so the __${...}__ preprocessing cannot carry expression syntax; no th:utext, no inline JavaScript, no unescaped sink was added.
Verb choice is correct for a destructive action: @PostMapping with a real HTML form, so the route is not reachable by GET, by link prefetch, or by an tag.

No secrets introduced. Swept the full change set for password/secret/token/apikey/credential/private_key: the only hit is prose in docs/system-design.md describing pre-existing datasource credential handling.

Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle is not in the change set, no dependency was added or upgraded, and no new transitive surface enters with this slice. (The project configures no dependencyCheck plugin, so no NVD scan was available to run — a pre-existing gap, not a finding against this change.)

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The new cancellation rule was deliberately placed on Visit.isUpcoming(), Pet.cancelVisit(), and Owner.cancelVisit() rather than in a controller specifically so it is 'testable without a servlet context' (ADR 2026-08-07-cancelling-a-visit-through-the-owner-aggregate.md, Consequences). Yet every test that exercises this logic boots a Spring context: the six behavior tests all run through @WebMvcTest MockMvc calls in VisitCancellationControllerTests, and the persistence test runs through @DataJpaTest in ClinicServiceTests. No plain JUnit test constructs a Visit/Pet/Owner directly and asserts on isUpcoming()/cancelVisit() without framework bootstrap. testing-principles.md § Test Pyramid asks exactly this question of a reviewer for a new rule: 'could this have been tested without booting the framework? If yes, it belongs in a unit and the test belongs in the base of the pyramid.' Here the answer is yes by the design's own rationale, but the pyramid gap was not closed — it was widened with more framework-booting tests.
findings.fix: Add plain JUnit unit tests (no @WebMvcTest/@DataJpaTest) that construct Visit/Pet/Owner directly and assert: Visit.isUpcoming() true for a future date, false for today and for a past date; Pet.cancelVisit() removes an upcoming visit and returns true, returns false and leaves the visit in place for a non-upcoming or unknown id; Owner.cancelVisit() delegates to the right pet and returns false for a pet id the owner does not hold. These can then anchor the existing MockMvc/DataJpaTest suites as their integration-level counterparts rather than the sole coverage.

findings.description: testing-principles.md § Test Data Construction (Factory Methods) requires that 'a slice adding a test writes it behind [a factory] from the start,' applying to tests written or modified from 2026-07-31 onward. theOwnerRecordShouldOfferCancelBesideAnUpcomingVisit (a wholly new test) constructs `new Visit()` and sets its fields directly instead of using a factory method; shouldDeleteTheRowOfACancelledVisit (also new) does the same. Both files already have precedent for raw construction in pre-existing tests, but that precedent predates the cutover and is not a license for new tests — the sibling new test class VisitCancellationControllerTests gets this right with its own visit(id, date, description) factory.
findings.fix: Add a small `visit(id, date, description)` (or `visitDatedFor(...)`) factory method to OwnerControllerTests and to ClinicServiceTests, mirroring the one in VisitCancellationControllerTests, and route the two new tests' Visit construction through it.

approved_aspects: All 10 REQ-VIS-003 acceptance criteria have a dedicated test: 6 in VisitCancellationControllerTests, 2 in OwnerControllerTests, 1 in ClinicServiceTests, and the language-completeness criterion via the pre-existing I18nPropertiesSyncTest.checkI18nPropertyFilesAreInSync, which now also enforces the new cancelVisit key across all ten non-English bundles.

shouldDeleteTheRowOfACancelledVisit genuinely guards the orphan-row defect: confirmed via the Hibernate SQL log from a full ./gradlew test run, which shows 'update visits set pet_id=null...' followed by 'delete from visits where id=?' with orphanRemoval=true. Without orphanRemoval only the UPDATE would fire, pet_id would be nulled but the row would remain, and the test's native COUNT(*) assertion would go from isZero() to observing 1 row -- red, as claimed.

VisitCancellationControllerTests exercises real Owner/Pet/Visit domain objects through MockMvc, mocking only OwnerRepository at the persistence boundary -- consistent with the brief's mocking policy and the sibling VisitControllerTests/OwnerControllerTests convention.

./gradlew test (86 tests) and jacocoTestReport pass; Owner, Visit, and VisitCancellationController show 100% line coverage and Pet 97% (the one miss is an unreachable defensive null check on a primitive int path variable).
